steps.message:
Item 051 on the Package A verification register is assigned to me and falls due on 07/20/2026, two days before the Level-3 placement. It covers the Block C spread footings and the long-term settlement of the clay beneath them.

Work through Item 051 against the project record and issue the verification memo. Set out what you reviewed, the basis you applied, your findings with the working behind them, and the disposition. Where something has to be produced before the item can be closed, say what it is and who is required to produce it.

Use the attached memorandum form and keep its sections. Write it from Rahul Nimkar, Geotechnical Reviewer, to Adrian Vance, Project Engineer, copied to Rachel Marlbeck. Save it as Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item051_BlockC.docx.

ROWAN BAY CONSTRUCTORS, INC.
4400 Alum Creek Drive, Columbus, OH 43207
Field Trailer — Birchwood Village, Package A
1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, OH 43210
FIELD MEMORANDUM
Field Memorandum — Level-2 Concrete Strength Non-Conformance (Set 3, Mix 03-CD-A)
1. Purpose
On review of the 07/06/2026 laboratory reports for the Level-2 slab, mix 03-CD-A specified at 5,000 psi, Set 3 (cast 05/26/2026) returned a 28-day average of 4,620 psi and a 7-day break of 3,150 psi. Both results fall below the specified f'c of 5,000 psi. Cylinder 4,180 psi is a failing individual test. In accordance with ACI 318-19 §26.12.3.1, we are treating Set 3 as a non-conforming placement and recommend rejection pending core testing.
2. Placement and Sample Reference
3. Result Summary
Specified strength: 5,000 psi. All three broken cylinders returned strengths below f'c. The 4,180 psi 28-day cylinder is a failing individual test. The 3,150 psi break at 7 days confirms early-age deficiency in the same placement. The 4,620 psi 28-day average is 380 psi below the 5,000 psi specified strength.
4. Basis for Non-Conformance
Set 3 of mix 03-CD-A is non-conforming to Specification 03 30 00 Article 3.7 and to ACI 318-19 §26.12.3.1. The 28-day average of 4,620 psi does not meet the 5,000 psi requirement, and the 4,180 psi individual break is a further failing result. Set 3 is accordingly flagged as a non-conforming placement.
5. Recommended Disposition
Reject Set 3 as placed pending confirmation by in-place core testing. We propose to core the placement per ACI 318-19 §26.12.3.4 after Thelbridge concurrence. Coring locations will be coordinated with Vantree Materials Testing and with Karen Tarbray so that neither the Level-2 slab surface finishes nor the Level-3 shoring layout is disturbed ahead of the 07/22/2026 Level-3 placement hold-point.
6. Schedule Impact
The Level-3 concrete placement is scheduled for 07/22/2026 (contractual hold-point). Coring, cure, and break time for three cores is on the order of 5–7 working days from the day cores are drilled. If coring authorization is issued this week, results can be in the record before the 07/22/2026 pour. Any slip in Thelbridge concurrence pushes the Level-3 hold-point at risk.
Please advise on Owner and Thelbridge concurrence at the earliest.
Marcus Whitfield
Superintendent, Rowan Bay Constructors, Inc.

Mobile: (614) 555-3302
mwhitfield@rowanbay.com

import openpyxl

def dump_xlsx(path, filter_str=None):
    print('====================================')
    print('XLSX:', path)
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=False)
    wb_val = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True)
    for name in wb.sheetnames:
        print('--- Sheet:', name)
        ws = wb[name]
        ws_val = wb_val[name]
        for r_idx in range(1, ws.max_row+1):
            row_f = [ws.cell(r_idx, c).value for c in range(1, ws.max_column+1)]
            row_v = [ws_val.cell(r_idx, c).value for c in range(1, ws_val.max_column+1)]
            if any(row_v):
                if row_f != row_v:
                    print(f'R{r_idx} VAL:', row_v)
                    print(f'R{r_idx} FRM:', row_f)
                else:
                    print(f'R{r_idx}:', row_v)

dump_xlsx('/filesystem/Birchwood/PackageA/02_Structural/Calcs/CB-GEO-007_Settlement_BlockC.xlsx')
dump_xlsx('/filesystem/Birchwood/PackageA/05_Field/Settlement_Monitoring_BlockC.xlsx')
dump_xlsx('/filesystem/Birchwood/PackageA/01_Geotech/Geotech_Index_Test_Data.xlsx')
dump_xlsx('/filesystem/Birchwood/PackageA/01_Geotech/Consolidation_Test_Data_D2435.xlsx')
"

ROWAN BAY CONSTRUCTORS, INC.
4400 Alum Creek Drive, Columbus, OH 43207
Field Trailer — Birchwood Village, Package A
1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, OH 43210
FIELD MEMORANDUM
Field Memorandum — Level-2 Concrete Strength Non-Conformance (Set 3, Mix 03-CD-A)
1. Purpose
On review of the 07/06/2026 laboratory reports for the Level-2 slab, mix 03-CD-A specified at 5,000 psi, Set 3 (cast 05/26/2026) returned a 28-day average of 4,620 psi and a 7-day break of 3,150 psi. Both results fall below the specified f'c of 5,000 psi. Cylinder 4,180 psi is a failing individual test. In accordance with ACI 318-19 §26.12.3.1, we are treating Set 3 as a non-conforming placement and recommend rejection pending core testing.
2. Placement and Sample Reference
3. Result Summary
Specified strength: 5,000 psi. All three broken cylinders returned strengths below f'c. The 4,180 psi 28-day cylinder is a failing individual test. The 3,150 psi break at 7 days confirms early-age deficiency in the same placement. The 4,620 psi 28-day average is 380 psi below the 5,000 psi specified strength.
4. Basis for Non-Conformance
Set 3 of mix 03-CD-A is non-conforming to Specification 03 30 00 Article 3.7 and to ACI 318-19 §26.12.3.1. The 28-day average of 4,620 psi does not meet the 5,000 psi requirement, and the 4,180 psi individual break is a further failing result. Set 3 is accordingly flagged as a non-conforming placement.
5. Recommended Disposition
Reject Set 3 as placed pending confirmation by in-place core testing. We propose to core the placement per ACI 318-19 §26.12.3.4 after Thelbridge concurrence. Coring locations will be coordinated with Vantree Materials Testing and with Karen Tarbray so that neither the Level-2 slab surface finishes nor the Level-3 shoring layout is disturbed ahead of the 07/22/2026 Level-3 placement hold-point.
6. Schedule Impact
The Level-3 concrete placement is scheduled for 07/22/2026 (contractual hold-point). Coring, cure, and break time for three cores is on the order of 5–7 working days from the day cores are drilled. If coring authorization is issued this week, results can be in the record before the 07/22/2026 pour. Any slip in Thelbridge concurrence pushes the Level-3 hold-point at risk.
Please advise on Owner and Thelbridge concurrence at the earliest.
Marcus Whitfield
Superintendent, Rowan Bay Constructors, Inc.

Mobile: (614) 555-3302
mwhitfield@rowanbay.com

wb = openpyxl.load_workbook('/filesystem/Birchwood/PackageA/02_Structural/Calcs/CB-GEO-007_Settlement_BlockC.xlsx', data_only=False)
wb_v = openpyxl.load_workbook('/filesystem/Birchwood/PackageA/02_Structural/Calcs/CB-GEO-007_Settlement_BlockC.xlsx', data_only=True)
for name in wb.sheetnames[:3]:
    print('=== Sheet:', name)
    ws, wsv = wb[name], wb_v[name]
    for r in range(1, ws.max_row+1):
        rf = [ws.cell(r, c).value for c in range(1, ws.max_column+1)]
        rv = [wsv.cell(r, c).value for c in range(1, wsv.max_column+1)]
        if any(rv):
            print(f'R{r}:', [x for x in rv if x is not None])

                print(f'R{r} F:', [x for x in rf if x is not None])
"

 1.  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

 Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. has completed a subsurface investigation and geotechnical engineering analysis for
 Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, Ohio.
 Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared podium, with
 a single basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
 Block B.
 The finished design grade across Package A is established at El. 750.0 ft. Existing ground surface stands at
 approximately El. 750.0 across the footprints of Blocks A and C but falls to about El. 738.0 across the Block B
 footprint (a former surface drainage swale). Placement of engineered fill of variable thickness — up to
 approximately 12 ft beneath Block B — will therefore be required to bring the site to design grade.
 The subsurface profile consists of three principal strata:
         Stratum 1 — Upper sand, classified SP-SM (poorly-graded sand with silt), medium-dense, from
       existing grade down to El. 738.0, total unit weight 118 pcf.
         Stratum 2 — Compressible clay aquitard, classified CL (lean clay of medium plasticity),
       normally-consolidated, from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 (18 ft thick), total unit weight 120 pcf, low
       permeability. This is the strata governing settlement of shallow foundations and provides the aquitard
       between the shallow and deep groundwater regimes.
         Stratum 3 — Dense sand and gravel aquifer, classified SW-GW, below El. 720.0, total unit weight 130
       pcf, confined by the overlying clay.
 Groundwater is present as two distinct regimes:
         The design water table in the upper sand is set at El. 742.0 ft. Piezometer readings taken from three
       shallow standpipes over the 11/2024–02/2025 monitoring period range from El. 741.6 to El. 742.4;
       groundwater seepage was observed at El. 741.8 to El. 742.2 in the Block A test-pit excavation.
         A confined piezometric head of El. 738.0 ft has been measured in the deep sand-and-gravel aquifer
       through two deep piezometers screened below El. 720.0, with readings ranging El. 737.7 to El. 738.3. The
       confined head is at essentially the same elevation as the top of the clay aquitard.
 Consolidation testing on two undisturbed Shelby-tube samples of the compressible clay (samples B-06 U3 and
 B-08 U2, tested per ASTM D2435) yielded a compression index Cc = 0.28, a recompression index Cr = 0.045,
 an initial void ratio e0 = 0.92, an in-situ vertical effective stress σ'0 = 1,850 psf, and a preconsolidation pressure
 σ'p = 1,900 psf. The margin (σ'p − σ'0 ≈ 50 psf) confirms the clay is essentially normally-consolidated: any net
 stress increase applied at the top of the clay will produce virgin (Cc) compression rather than recompression
 (Cr) compression.
 Principal geotechnical recommendations are as follows:

 1.  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

 Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. has completed a subsurface investigation and geotechnical engineering analysis for
 Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, Ohio.
 Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared podium, with
 a single basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
 Block B.
 The finished design grade across Package A is established at El. 750.0 ft. Existing ground surface stands at
 approximately El. 750.0 across the footprints of Blocks A and C but falls to about El. 738.0 across the Block B
 footprint (a former surface drainage swale). Placement of engineered fill of variable thickness — up to
 approximately 12 ft beneath Block B — will therefore be required to bring the site to design grade.
 The subsurface profile consists of three principal strata:
         Stratum 1 — Upper sand, classified SP-SM (poorly-graded sand with silt), medium-dense, from
       existing grade down to El. 738.0, total unit weight 118 pcf.
         Stratum 2 — Compressible clay aquitard, classified CL (lean clay of medium plasticity),
       normally-consolidated, from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 (18 ft thick), total unit weight 120 pcf, low
       permeability. This is the strata governing settlement of shallow foundations and provides the aquitard
       between the shallow and deep groundwater regimes.
         Stratum 3 — Dense sand and gravel aquifer, classified SW-GW, below El. 720.0, total unit weight 130
       pcf, confined by the overlying clay.
 Groundwater is present as two distinct regimes:
         The design water table in the upper sand is set at El. 742.0 ft. Piezometer readings taken from three
       shallow standpipes over the 11/2024–02/2025 monitoring period range from El. 741.6 to El. 742.4;
       groundwater seepage was observed at El. 741.8 to El. 742.2 in the Block A test-pit excavation.
         A confined piezometric head of El. 738.0 ft has been measured in the deep sand-and-gravel aquifer
       through two deep piezometers screened below El. 720.0, with readings ranging El. 737.7 to El. 738.3. The
       confined head is at essentially the same elevation as the top of the clay aquitard.
 Consolidation testing on two undisturbed Shelby-tube samples of the compressible clay (samples B-06 U3 and
 B-08 U2, tested per ASTM D2435) yielded a compression index Cc = 0.28, a recompression index Cr = 0.045,
 an initial void ratio e0 = 0.92, an in-situ vertical effective stress σ'0 = 1,850 psf, and a preconsolidation pressure
 σ'p = 1,900 psf. The margin (σ'p − σ'0 ≈ 50 psf) confirms the clay is essentially normally-consolidated: any net
 stress increase applied at the top of the clay will produce virgin (Cc) compression rather than recompression
 (Cr) compression.
 Principal geotechnical recommendations are as follows:
        1.  Block C — Spread footings may be founded within the upper sand. Consolidation of the underlying
        compressible clay under column-load stress increases at mid-depth of the clay must be explicitly computed
        by the Structural Engineer of Record, using the parameters provided herein, and reconciled against the
        settlement tolerances specified in the project structural criteria.
        2.  Blocks A and B basement mat — A conventional reinforced-concrete mat foundation may be founded
        within the upper sand at the design underside elevation. Hydrostatic uplift from the El. 742.0 water table
        must be resolved by mat self-weight, superimposed permanent loads and, where necessary, tension
        elements. The waterproofing system for the below-grade envelope must be selected for the applicable

[page 8]

        hydrostatic head.
        3.  Block B piles — Because of anticipated fill-induced consolidation of the underlying clay and the
        resulting downdrag loads, and because column loads at Block B exceed the safe capacity of shallow
        foundations bearing on the upper sand, closed-end driven pipe piles carried through the upper sand and the
        clay to bearing in the dense sand and gravel aquifer below El. 720.0 are recommended. The pile design
        must address soil-pile interaction from clay consolidation, as the engineered fill load induces downdrag on
        piles driven through the consolidating clay (Section 8.3).
        4.  Block B plant-room excavation — The plant-room subgrade is planned near El. 726.0, i.e., inside the
        clay aquitard, approximately 6 ft above the top of the confined aquifer at El. 720.0. Because the confined
        piezometric head (El. 738.0) is approximately 12 ft above the planned subgrade elevation, this excavation
        will develop a significant uplift pressure on the clay plug from the underlying aquifer.
        The base-heave stability of the plug must be evaluated by the design team, and pressure-relief
        or aquifer-drawdown measures may be required. This condition is called out as the controlling
        constructability issue for the plant-room excavation and must be addressed by the Contractor’s dewatering
        and shoring designs.
        5.  Engineered fill over the clay — The 12 ft of engineered fill required beneath Block B (from El. 738.0
        up to El. 750.0) will constitute a net surcharge on the normally-consolidated compressible clay across the
        Block B footprint. Because σ'p ≈ σ'0, the entire increment is virgin compression under Cc. The Owner is
        advised that consolidation of the underlying clay under this fill surcharge will occur, that the associated
        settlement will affect the behavior of any deep foundations driven from the raised working grade before
        the consolidation is substantially complete, and that these effects must be considered in the pile design.

Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. has completed a subsurface investigation and geotechnical engineering analysis for
Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, Ohio.
Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared podium, with
a single basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
Block B.
The finished design grade across Package A is established at El. 750.0 ft. Existing ground surface stands at
approximately El. 750.0 across the footprints of Blocks A and C but falls to about El. 738.0 across the Block B
footprint (a former surface drainage swale). Placement of engineered fill of variable thickness — up to
approximately 12 ft beneath Block B — will therefore be required to bring the site to design grade.
The subsurface profile consists of three principal strata:
•  Stratum 1 — Upper sand, classified SP-SM (poorly-graded sand with silt), medium-dense, from
existing grade down to El. 738.0, total unit weight 118 pcf.
•  Stratum 2 — Compressible clay aquitard, classified CL (lean clay of medium plasticity),
normally-consolidated, from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 (18 ft thick), total unit weight 120 pcf, low
permeability. This is the strata governing settlement of shallow foundations and provides the aquitard
between the shallow and deep groundwater regimes.
•  Stratum 3 — Dense sand and gravel aquifer, classified SW-GW, below El. 720.0, total unit weight 130
pcf, confined by the overlying clay.
Groundwater is present as two distinct regimes:
•  The design water table in the upper sand is set at El. 742.0 ft. Piezometer readings taken from three
shallow standpipes over the 11/2024–02/2025 monitoring period range from El. 741.6 to El. 742.4;

surficial geology is dominated by Wisconsinan-age glacial deposits — chiefly clay-rich till, glaciolacustrine silt
and clay, and outwash sand and gravel — overlying Devonian-age carbonate and shale bedrock. Local
hydrogeology is characterized by a shallow phreatic surface within the outwash and reworked outwash sands, a
laterally continuous fine-grained aquitard, and a lower confined aquifer within basal outwash sand and gravel
above bedrock.
The subsurface conditions encountered in the Package A borings are consistent with this regional framework: a
medium-dense reworked outwash sand at the surface, a low-permeability clay of glaciolacustrine origin at
intermediate depth, and a dense outwash sand and gravel aquifer at depth. Bedrock was not encountered within
the maximum boring depth of 90 ft (approximately El. 660.0). Blow counts in the SW-GW below El. 720.0
were consistently in the range N ≥ 50 blows per 6 inches, indicating a very dense sand-and-gravel deposit
suitable as a pile-bearing stratum.
3.3  Site History and Prior Use
Site historical review — including review of Franklin County parcel records, USGS topographic maps (1955
and later editions), and Thornbury State University campus master planning archives — indicates that the
Package A parcel was in agricultural use through approximately 1958, was acquired by the University in 1962,
and has been used for surface parking and landscape maintenance since. No prior structures of consequence, no
known below-grade utilities (other than a single abandoned 6-inch clay drain traced along the historic swale in
Block B), and no known industrial fill are present within the footprint. Because there is essentially no prior fill
of engineering significance, the Block B footprint requires new engineered fill — placed on the natural
clay-upper-sand contact after removal of the topsoil mantle — to bring the site to design grade.

import pymupdf, math

for p in [
    '/filesystem/Birchwood/PackageA/02_Structural/Drawings/S-101_Foundation_Plan_Rev4.pdf',
    '/filesystem/Birchwood/PackageA/02_Structural/Drawings/S-201_Foundation_Sections_Details_Rev4.pdf',
]:
    txt = pymupdf.open(p)[0].get_text()
    idx = txt.find('BLOCK C') if 'BLOCK C' in txt else txt.find('3/S-201')
    print('===', p, '===')
    print(txt[max(0, idx-100):idx+1500])

doc_b = pymupdf.open('/filesystem/Birchwood/PackageA/01_Geotech/Boring_Logs_and_GW_Monitoring_B01-B09.pdf')
for pg in doc_b:
    t = pg.get_text()
    if 'BORING LOG — B-06' in t:
        print('=== B-06 ===')
        print(t)

# Consolidation calculations
Cc = 0.28
Cr = 0.045
e0 = 0.92
H_ft = 18.0
H_in = 216.0
sigma0 = 1850.0
sigmap = 1900.0
dsigma = 900.0
sigmaf = sigma0 + dsigma

# Pure virgin (Kelbrook GIR eq 8.1: Sc = Cc * H / (1+e0) * log10((sigma0 + q)/sigma0))
Sc_virgin_ft = (Cc * H_ft / (1 + e0)) * math.log10((sigma0 + dsigma) / sigma0)
Sc_virgin_in = Sc_virgin_ft * 12

# Two-branch (Cr from 1850 to 1900, Cc from 1900 to 2750)
Sc_2branch_ft = (H_ft / (1 + e0)) * (Cr * math.log10(sigmap / sigma0) + Cc * math.log10(sigmaf / sigmap))
Sc_2branch_in = Sc_2branch_ft * 12

print(f'Sc_virgin: {Sc_virgin_ft:.4f} ft = {Sc_virgin_in:.2f} in ({Sc_virgin_in:.4f} in)')
print(f'Sc_2branch: {Sc_2branch_ft:.4f} ft = {Sc_2branch_in:.2f} in ({Sc_2branch_in:.4f} in)')
"

Please close the current list — the shoring for the August Block B excavation, the pile downdrag question, the mat buoyancy check, Block C long-term settlement, this week's rebar lot and concrete breaks, the slab-on-grade compaction results, the podium deflection check, the basement seepage assessment, and the reinforcement cover on foundation and exterior work — and let me know by 07/20/2026 which are cleared and which are not.

Steven.

1.  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. has completed a subsurface investigation and geotechnical engineering analysis for
Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, Ohio.
Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared podium, with
a single basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
Block B.
The finished design grade across Package A is established at El. 750.0 ft. Existing ground surface stands at
approximately El. 750.0 across the footprints of Blocks A and C but falls to about El. 738.0 across the Block B
footprint (a former surface drainage swale). Placement of engineered fill of variable thickness — up to
approximately 12 ft beneath Block B — will therefore be required to bring the site to design grade.
The subsurface profile consists of three principal strata:
•  Stratum 1 — Upper sand, classified SP-SM (poorly-graded sand with silt), medium-dense, from
existing grade down to El. 738.0, total unit weight 118 pcf.
•  Stratum 2 — Compressible clay aquitard, classified CL (lean clay of medium plasticity),
normally-consolidated, from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 (18 ft thick), total unit weight 120 pcf, low
permeability. This is the strata governing settlement of shallow foundations and provides the aquitard
between the shallow and deep groundwater regimes.
•  Stratum 3 — Dense sand and gravel aquifer, classified SW-GW, below El. 720.0, total unit weight 130
pcf, confined by the overlying clay.
Groundwater is present as two distinct regimes:
•  The design water table in the upper sand is set at El. 742.0 ft. Piezometer readings taken from three
shallow standpipes over the 11/2024–02/2025 monitoring period range from El. 741.6 to El. 742.4;
groundwater seepage was observed at El. 741.8 to El. 742.2 in the Block A test-pit excavation.
•  A confined piezometric head of El. 738.0 ft has been measured in the deep sand-and-gravel aquifer
through two deep piezometers screened below El. 720.0, with readings ranging El. 737.7 to El. 738.3. The
confined head is at essentially the same elevation as the top of the clay aquitard.
Consolidation testing on two undisturbed Shelby-tube samples of the compressible clay (samples B-06 U3 and
B-08 U2, tested per ASTM D2435) yielded a compression index Cc = 0.28, a recompression index Cr = 0.045,
an initial void ratio e0 = 0.92, an in-situ vertical effective stress σ'0 = 1,850 psf, and a preconsolidation pressure
σ'p = 1,900 psf. The margin (σ'p − σ'0 ≈ 50 psf) confirms the clay is essentially normally-consolidated: any net
stress increase applied at the top of the clay will produce virgin (Cc) compression rather than recompression
(Cr) compression.

settlement tolerances specified in the project structural criteria.

within the upper sand at the design underside elevation. Hydrostatic uplift from the El. 742.0 water table

3.2  Regional and Local Geology
Columbus, Ohio lies within the Till Plains section of the Central Lowland physiographic province. Regional
surficial geology is dominated by Wisconsinan-age glacial deposits — chiefly clay-rich till, glaciolacustrine silt
and clay, and outwash sand and gravel — overlying Devonian-age carbonate and shale bedrock. Local
hydrogeology is characterized by a shallow phreatic surface within the outwash and reworked outwash sands, a
laterally continuous fine-grained aquitard, and a lower confined aquifer within basal outwash sand and gravel
above bedrock.
The subsurface conditions encountered in the Package A borings are consistent with this regional framework: a
medium-dense reworked outwash sand at the surface, a low-permeability clay of glaciolacustrine origin at
intermediate depth, and a dense outwash sand and gravel aquifer at depth. Bedrock was not encountered within
the maximum boring depth of 90 ft (approximately El. 660.0). Blow counts in the SW-GW below El. 720.0
were consistently in the range N ≥ 50 blows per 6 inches, indicating a very dense sand-and-gravel deposit
suitable as a pile-bearing stratum.
3.3  Site History and Prior Use
Site historical review — including review of Franklin County parcel records, USGS topographic maps (1955
and later editions), and Thornbury State University campus master planning archives — indicates that the
Package A parcel was in agricultural use through approximately 1958, was acquired by the University in 1962,
and has been used for surface parking and landscape maintenance since. No prior structures of consequence, no
known below-grade utilities (other than a single abandoned 6-inch clay drain traced along the historic swale in
Block B), and no known industrial fill are present within the footprint. Because there is essentially no prior fill
of engineering significance, the Block B footprint requires new engineered fill — placed on the natural
clay-upper-sand contact after removal of the topsoil mantle — to bring the site to design grade.

7.2  Confined Piezometric Head — Deep Aquifer
Groundwater within the deep SW-GW sand and gravel aquifer is confined by the CL clay aquitard. Piezometric
head measured in the two deep piezometers (screened below El. 720.0 in Borings B-04 and B-08) is at El. 738.0

discharges downstream through the same continuous outwash body; the clay acts as an aquitard that prevents
equalization of the two heads. The confined piezometric head of El. 738.0 is the elevation to which water will
rise in any well, boring or excavation that penetrates the clay and exposes the underlying aquifer. Any
excavation that either (a) penetrates the clay and enters the aquifer, or (b) reduces the effective weight of the
clay plug between the excavation subgrade and the top of the aquifer, will be subject to upward hydrostatic
pressure equal to the confined head above the point in question.

The Block B footprint is raised approximately 12 ft above its natural surface by engineered fill placed
over a normally-consolidated CLAY 18 ft thick and of low permeability. Primary consolidation of that
clay under the weight of the new fill was in progress at the date of this issue and, on the coefficients

months.
Deep foundations driven from the raised working grade pass through that consolidating layer. Where the
surrounding soil settles more than the pile, the relative movement at the pile-soil interface reverses:
the soil moves down past the shaft instead of the shaft moving down past the soil.
Over the depth in which that condition applies the interface shear acts downward on the pile. It is an
additional axial load carried by the pile, not a component of its resistance, and it is superimposed on
the structural load for as long as consolidation continues.
The magnitude depends on the thickness of the still-consolidating layer, the interface shear available
within it and the depth of the neutral plane. Requirements for its treatment in design are set out in
Section 9.3.

A.   Common fill placed outside the building envelope shall be free of organic material, debris, and
frozen soil, but is not subject to the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B.
2.3   CAPILLARY BREAK / DRAINAGE COURSE
A.   Clean, open-graded crushed stone, 3/4 in nominal, less than 2% passing the No. 200 sieve,
placed as shown on the Drawings beneath slabs-on-grade.
PART 3    EXECUTION
3.1   EXAMINATION
A.   Examine subgrade prior to fill placement. Do not proceed with fill placement over subgrade
that is soft, yielding under proof roll, frozen, or otherwise unsuitable. Notify the Owner's
Representative Engineer in writing of any unsuitable subgrade condition.
3.2   SUBGRADE PREPARATION
A.   Strip topsoil, organic material, and any existing uncontrolled fill from beneath the footprint of
structural fill.
B.   Proof-roll exposed subgrade with a loaded tandem-axle dump truck or equivalent equipment
approved in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer. The Laboratory shall be present

to witness the proof roll.
C.   Undercut and replace yielding areas with structural fill placed and compacted per this
Section.
3.3   PLACEMENT
A.   Place structural fill in horizontal lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose thickness.
B.   Moisture-condition each lift, by wetting or drying and mixing, so that the moisture content at
the time of compaction is within the range specified in Article 3.4.B.
C.   Compact each lift with equipment sized and operated to achieve the density and moisture
requirements of Article 3.4.B throughout the full thickness of the lift.
D.   Do not place fill on frozen subgrade or with frozen material. Do not place fill during
precipitation that raises the placed material's moisture content above the upper limit of Article
3.4.B.
3.4   COMPACTION
A.   Method Statement. The Contractor shall place structural fill in controlled lifts as specified in
Article 3.3, moisture-conditioning each lift as necessary to bring the material within the
moisture range required by Article 3.4.B before compaction. Compaction equipment
(self-propelled vibratory smooth-drum rollers, pad-foot rollers, or plate compactors adjacent to
structures) shall be operated in a pattern of overlapping passes such that every location
within a lift receives no fewer than the number of passes established during a
Contractor-conducted test strip witnessed by the Laboratory and the Owner's Representative
Engineer. The test strip shall be executed at the start of production placement, using the
placement source, moisture-conditioning method, lift thickness, and compaction equipment
intended for production, and shall demonstrate that the criteria of Article 3.4.B are met before
general production is authorized. Adjacent to walls, columns, and utilities, use hand-operated
compaction equipment in lifts not exceeding 6 inches loose thickness. Do not operate heavy
compaction equipment within 3 feet of walls prior to backfill balancing on both sides. Each lift
shall be tested and accepted per Article 3.4.B before the next lift is placed.
B.   Acceptance Criteria.
Structural fill shall be placed and compacted to a dry density of not less than
95% of the maximum dry density determined by ASTM D1557 Method C for the
placed material, AND shall be placed at a moisture content within −1% to +2%
of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must
be satisfied for each test location. Field density shall be measured per ASTM
D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode) at a frequency of one test per
5,000 sf per lift.
C.   Failing Tests. Where either the density criterion or the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B is
not satisfied at any test location:
1.   The affected area of the lift shall be reworked (scarified, moisture-conditioned, and
recompacted, or removed and replaced) at the Contractor's expense.
2.   Reworked areas shall be retested by the Laboratory. Both the density and moisture
criteria of Article 3.4.B must be satisfied on the retest before the lift is accepted.

3.   Isolated failing tests may not be averaged with adjacent passing tests to demonstrate
compliance. Acceptance is evaluated at each test location independently.
D.   Interpretation. No test location shall be accepted on the basis of density alone. No test
location shall be accepted on the basis of moisture alone. Compliance requires that both the
density criterion and the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B be independently satisfied at that
test location, as measured against the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry
density and optimum moisture content of the material actually placed at that location.
3.5   BACKFILL AGAINST FOUNDATION WALLS
A.   Do not commence backfill against basement or foundation walls until the wall has attained its
specified 28-day compressive strength, or until permanent lateral support (floor framing) is in
place and grouted to the wall, whichever occurs first.
B.   Place backfill on both sides of interior walls in balanced lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose
thickness, differing by no more than one lift side-to-side.
C.   Compact backfill to the same acceptance criteria as Article 3.4.B where the backfill supports
structure or slabs; elsewhere, to 90% of ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density.
3.6   SETTLEMENT TOLERANCE
A.   Total and Differential Settlement. Total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement
0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.
B.   Application. The tolerances of Paragraph A apply to the completed foundation system as
constructed on the accepted subgrade and structural fill delivered under this Section. Where
predicted or monitored settlements exceed the tolerances of Paragraph A, the Structural
Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a
written disposition is issued.
C.   Monitoring. Where settlement monitoring points are shown on the Drawings, readings shall
be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the frequency indicated.
Cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance of Paragraph A shall be reported
immediately.
3.7   FIELD QUALITY CONTROL
A.   Testing frequency for structural fill:
1.   In-place density and moisture: one ASTM D6938 test per 5,000 sf per lift, as required by
Article 3.4.B, and not fewer than three tests per lift regardless of lift area.
2.   Laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content: one ASTM D1557
Method C determination per source, and one additional determination for each material
change identified by visual classification or gradation.
B.   Reporting. The Laboratory shall issue field density reports within 24 hours of testing. Each
report shall identify, for each test location, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum
dry density and optimum moisture content used as the denominators, the measured dry
density, the measured moisture content, the percent compaction, the moisture deviation from
optimum, and the disposition (accept or reject) against Article 3.4.B.
C.   Non-Conforming Work. Any lift not meeting Article 3.4.B, or any lift for which the ASTM
D1557 Method C denominators used in reporting do not correspond to the material actually
placed, shall be reworked as required by Article 3.4.C before any additional lift is placed.

A.   Protect accepted subgrade and completed structural fill from disturbance, softening by
precipitation, freezing, and construction traffic until covered by permanent construction.
Rework and retest, at the Contractor's expense, any area disturbed or softened prior to
permanent cover.

and clay, and outwash sand and gravel — overlying Devonian-age carbonate and shale bedrock. Local
hydrogeology is characterized by a shallow phreatic surface within the outwash and reworked outwash sands, a
laterally continuous fine-grained aquitard, and a lower confined aquifer within basal outwash sand and gravel
above bedrock.
The subsurface conditions encountered in the Package A borings are consistent with this regional framework: a
medium-dense reworked outwash sand at the surface, a low-permeability clay of glaciolacustrine origin at
intermediate depth, and a dense outwash sand and gravel aquifer at depth. Bedrock was not encountered within
the maximum boring depth of 90 ft (approximately El. 660.0). Blow counts in the SW-GW below El. 720.0
were consistently in the range N ≥ 50 blows per 6 inches, indicating a very dense sand-and-gravel deposit
suitable as a pile-bearing stratum.
3.3  Site History and Prior Use
Site historical review — including review of Franklin County parcel records, USGS topographic maps (1955
and later editions), and Thornbury State University campus master planning archives — indicates that the
Package A parcel was in agricultural use through approximately 1958, was acquired by the University in 1962,
and has been used for surface parking and landscape maintenance since. No prior structures of consequence, no
known below-grade utilities (other than a single abandoned 6-inch clay drain traced along the historic swale in
Block B), and no known industrial fill are present within the footprint. Because there is essentially no prior fill
of engineering significance, the Block B footprint requires new engineered fill — placed on the natural
clay-upper-sand contact after removal of the topsoil mantle — to bring the site to design grade.

1.3   DEFINITIONS
A.   Structural Fill: Imported or on-site engineered soil placed and compacted in controlled lifts
beneath building foundations, mat foundations, pile caps, footings, or slabs-on-grade, and
meeting the material, gradation, and compaction requirements of this Section.
B.   Common Fill: Non-structural earth used only for site grading outside the building envelope.
C.   Lift: A single layer of loose fill placed in preparation for compaction, not exceeding the
maximum loose lift thickness specified in Part 3.
D.   Test Location: A single field-density test point at which both dry density and moisture
content are measured for compliance evaluation.
E.   Placed Material: The specific soil material actually placed in the field at the test location,
whose laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content have been established
by ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory testing prior to placement, as required by Article 2.1.
1.4   QUALITY ASSURANCE
A.   Testing Laboratory. Field and laboratory testing under this Section shall be performed by the
Owner's independent construction materials testing laboratory (the “Laboratory”), contracted
directly to the Owner. The Contractor shall coordinate access, sampling opportunity, and
lift-by-lift notification with the Laboratory.
B.   Personnel. Nuclear-gauge operators shall hold current radiation safety training and shall be
documented as competent in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures. Nuclear gauges
shall be calibrated within the manufacturer's stated interval and standard-count checked at
the start of each testing day.
C.   Placed-Material Correspondence. The laboratory maximum dry density and optimum
moisture content used as the acceptance denominators for any test location shall be those
determined by ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually placed at that location. Where
the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow, a new ASTM
D1557 Method C test shall be performed on the new material before further fill placement is
accepted.

3.3   PLACEMENT
A.   Place structural fill in horizontal lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose thickness.
B.   Moisture-condition each lift, by wetting or drying and mixing, so that the moisture content at
the time of compaction is within the range specified in Article 3.4.B.
C.   Compact each lift with equipment sized and operated to achieve the density and moisture

D.   Do not place fill on frozen subgrade or with frozen material. Do not place fill during
precipitation that raises the placed material's moisture content above the upper limit of Article
3.4.B.
3.4   COMPACTION
A.   Method Statement. The Contractor shall place structural fill in controlled lifts as specified in
Article 3.3, moisture-conditioning each lift as necessary to bring the material within the
moisture range required by Article 3.4.B before compaction. Compaction equipment
(self-propelled vibratory smooth-drum rollers, pad-foot rollers, or plate compactors adjacent to
structures) shall be operated in a pattern of overlapping passes such that every location
within a lift receives no fewer than the number of passes established during a
Contractor-conducted test strip witnessed by the Laboratory and the Owner's Representative
Engineer. The test strip shall be executed at the start of production placement, using the
placement source, moisture-conditioning method, lift thickness, and compaction equipment
intended for production, and shall demonstrate that the criteria of Article 3.4.B are met before
general production is authorized. Adjacent to walls, columns, and utilities, use hand-operated
compaction equipment in lifts not exceeding 6 inches loose thickness. Do not operate heavy
compaction equipment within 3 feet of walls prior to backfill balancing on both sides. Each lift
shall be tested and accepted per Article 3.4.B before the next lift is placed.
B.   Acceptance Criteria.
Structural fill shall be placed and compacted to a dry density of not less than
95% of the maximum dry density determined by ASTM D1557 Method C for the
placed material, AND shall be placed at a moisture content within −1% to +2%
of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must
be satisfied for each test location. Field density shall be measured per ASTM
D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode) at a frequency of one test per
5,000 sf per lift.
C.   Failing Tests. Where either the density criterion or the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B is
not satisfied at any test location:
1.   The affected area of the lift shall be reworked (scarified, moisture-conditioned, and
recompacted, or removed and replaced) at the Contractor's expense.
2.   Reworked areas shall be retested by the Laboratory. Both the density and moisture
criteria of Article 3.4.B must be satisfied on the retest before the lift is accepted.

compliance. Acceptance is evaluated at each test location independently.
D.   Interpretation. No test location shall be accepted on the basis of density alone. No test
location shall be accepted on the basis of moisture alone. Compliance requires that both the
density criterion and the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B be independently satisfied at that
test location, as measured against the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry
density and optimum moisture content of the material actually placed at that location.

A.   Do not commence backfill against basement or foundation walls until the wall has attained its
specified 28-day compressive strength, or until permanent lateral support (floor framing) is in
place and grouted to the wall, whichever occurs first.
B.   Place backfill on both sides of interior walls in balanced lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose
thickness, differing by no more than one lift side-to-side.

The verification review of **Item 051** on the Birchwood Village Expansion — Package A Verification Register has been completed against the project record, and the updated Verification Memorandum has been saved and verified on disk.

### Deliverable Summary
- **Deliverable Path:** `/filesystem/Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item051_BlockC.docx`
- **Template & Structure Preserved:** Generated from `/filesystem/Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_TEMPLATE_v1.docx`, preserving the letterhead (`THELBRIDGE PROJECT MANAGEMENT SERVICES`), memorandum header block, all five numbered sections (`1.  PURPOSE`, `2.  DOCUMENTS REVIEWED`, `3.  BASIS OF REVIEW`, `4.  FINDINGS`, `5.  CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION`), and the signature block.
- **Scope Exclusion Applied:** Explicitly focuses verification on **Item 051** on the Package A verification register covering the Block C spread footings and the long-term consolidation settlement of the clay beneath them, rather than unrelated Package A verification items (e.g., Block B piles/fill, Level 2 slab deflection, rebar/concrete breaks, or basement waterproofing leaks) except where cross-referenced by the Item 051 record, and removes any disallowed comma between specification section numbers and titles/articles (`Specification Section 31 20 00 Article 3.6.B`).
- **Header & Sign-Off Metadata:**
  - **To:** Adrian Vance, Project Engineer (Structural/Geotechnical), Owner's Representative — Thelbridge Project Management Services
  - **From:** Rahul Nimkar, Geotechnical Reviewer — Thelbridge Project Management Services
  - **CC:** Rachel Marlbeck, University Program Director — Thornbury State University, Office of Capital Programs
  - **Date:** `07/20/2026` (`2026-07-20`, two days before the scheduled `07/22/2026` Level-3 concrete placement)
  - **Subject:** Package A Verification Register Item 051 — Block C Spread Footings and Long-Term Clay Consolidation Settlement

---

### Summary of Verified Findings & Numerical Working

1. **Subsurface Profile, In-Situ Stress State, and Laboratory Consolidation Parameters (`KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2`, `Boring_Logs_and_GW_Monitoring_B01-B09.pdf`, `Geotech_Index_Test_Data.xlsx`, `VMT-2025-0109-CON`):**
   - Beneath Block C (grade $\text{El. } 750.0\text{ ft}$; Boring B-09 at $\text{El. } 749.9\text{ ft}$), Stratum 1 medium-dense SP-SM sand ($\gamma_1 = 118\text{ pcf}$, design water table $\text{El. } 742.0\text{ ft}$) extends to $\text{El. } 738.0\text{ ft}$, underlain by Stratum 2 compressible lean clay aquitard (USCS CL, $\text{El. } 738.0\text{ ft}$ to $\text{El. } 720.0\text{ ft}$, thickness $H = 18.0\text{ ft} = 216\text{ in}$, $\gamma_2 = 120\text{ pcf}$) and Stratum 3 dense SW-GW sand and gravel below $\text{El. } 720.0\text{ ft}$ ($\gamma_3 = 130\text{ pcf}$, confined piezometric head $\text{El. } 738.0\text{ ft}$, double-drained boundaries with $H_{\text{dr}} = 9.0\text{ ft}$).
   - ASTM D2435 oedometer testing (`VMT-2025-0109-CON`, Talia Brennard, PE, `01/09/2025`) on undisturbed Shelby-tube samples B-06 U3 ($\text{El. } 729.5\text{ ft}$, depth $10.0\text{–}12.5\text{ ft}$) and B-08 U2 ($\text{El. } 728.7\text{ ft}$, depth $7.5\text{–}10.0\text{ ft}$) established: $C_c = 0.28$, $C_r = 0.045$, $e_0 = 0.92$, in-situ vertical effective stress $\sigma'_0 = 1,850\text{ psf}$ at mid-depth ($\text{El. } 729.0\text{ ft}$), Casagrande preconsolidation pressure $\sigma'_p = 1,900\text{ psf}$ ($\text{OCR} = 1.03$, margin $\sigma'_p - \sigma'_0 = 50\text{ psf}$), and virgin coefficient of consolidation $c_v = 4.5 \times 10^{-4}\text{ cm}^2/\text{s} \approx 0.042\text{ ft}^2/\text{day}$.

2. **Critical Omission in Calculation `CB-GEO-007` (Rev.0, `09/30/2025`):**
   - On Sheet 2 of `CB-GEO-007`, Calloway Braddock (Gregory Nash, PE) establishes Block C spread-footing service loads (F-C1 through F-C12, $8.5\text{ ft} \times 8.5\text{ ft}$ to $10.5\text{ ft} \times 10.5\text{ ft}$, $q_{\text{net}} = 3,450\text{ to }3,730\text{ psf}$) and a combined Boussinesq/Newmark vertical stress increase at mid-clay ($\text{El. } 729.0\text{ ft}$) of $\Delta\sigma = 900\text{ psf}$.
   - On Sheet 3, the EOR computes only immediate elastic settlement by the Schmertmann method ($S_i = 0.70\text{ to }0.90\text{ in}$, maximum $0.90\text{ in}$ at F-C6, $0.82\text{ in}$ at F-C7, maximum differential $\Delta S_i = 0.20\text{ in}$), which already consumes $90\%$ of the $1.0\text{ in}$ total settlement limit.
   - On **Sheet 4 (Consolidation)**, every consolidation entry ($\sigma'_0, \Delta\sigma, \sigma'_p, H, C_c, e_0, \text{Result}$) is left blank (`—`) with the note: *"Not computed. Serviceability taken from the immediate settlement result on Sheet 3,"* while Sheet 5 merely lists the Vantree parameters *"for the record and to close out the transmittal."* This directly violates `KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2` Section 1 (p. 6) and Section 9.1 (pp. 16–17). In addition, `CB-GEO-007` Sheet 2 uses a footing base elevation of $\text{El. } 740.5\text{ ft}$ ($2.5\text{ ft}$ above top of clay), whereas Structural Drawing `S-201 Rev.4` Detail 3/S-201 specifies $\text{El. } 746.0\text{ ft}$.

3. **Independent Computation of Primary Consolidation ($S_c$), Total ($S_{\text{total}}$), and Differential Settlement:**
   - With $H / (1 + e_0) = 18.0\text{ ft} / 1.92 = 9.375\text{ ft} = 112.50\text{ in}$, $\sigma'_0 = 1,850\text{ psf}$, $\sigma'_p = 1,900\text{ psf}$, and $\sigma'_f = \sigma'_0 + \Delta\sigma = 2,750\text{ psf}$:
     - **Exact Two-Branch (Recompression + Virgin) Consolidation Settlement:**
       $$S_c = 112.50\text{ in} \times \left[0.045 \log_{10}\!\left(\frac{1,900}{1,850}\right) + 0.28 \log_{10}\!\left(\frac{2,750}{1,900}\right)\right] = 0.0586\text{ in} + 5.0582\text{ in} = \mathbf{5.12\text{ in}}\text{ (}0.426\text{ ft)}$$
     - **Single-Branch Normally-Consolidated Virgin Equation (`KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2` Section 8.1, p. 14):**
       $$S_c = 112.50\text{ in} \times 0.28 \log_{10}\!\left(\frac{2,750}{1,850}\right) = 31.50\text{ in} \times 0.172161 = \mathbf{5.42\text{ in}}\text{ (}0.452\text{ ft)}$$
     - **Combined Total Settlement ($S_{\text{total}} = S_i + S_c$ at F-C6):**
       $$S_{\text{total}} = 0.90\text{ in} + 5.12\text{ in} = \mathbf{6.02\text{ in}}\text{ (bilinear)} \quad \text{or} \quad 0.90\text{ in} + 5.42\text{ in} = \mathbf{6.32\text{ in}}\text{ (single-branch NC)}$$
     - **Exceedance of Project Limits:** Primary consolidation settlement alone ($5.12\text{ to }5.42\text{ in}$) exceeds the **$1.0\text{ in}$ maximum total settlement tolerance** by more than **$5\times$** ($512\%\text{–}542\%$), and combined total settlement ($6.02\text{ to }6.32\text{ in}$) exceeds the limit by over $5.0\text{ in}$. Long-term differential settlement between interior footings (F-C6/F-C7) and edge/corner footings reaches **$1.36\text{ to }2.50\text{ in}$** ($272\%\text{–}500\%$ of the **$0.5\text{ in}$ maximum differential settlement limit**, violating the $1/500$ angular distortion limit).

4. **Time-Rate of Consolidation and Correlation with Field Monitoring (`Settlement_Monitoring_BlockC.xlsx`):**
   - For double drainage ($H_{\text{dr}} = 9.0\text{ ft}$, $H_{\text{dr}}^2 = 81.0\text{ ft}^2$) and $c_v = 0.042\text{ ft}^2/\text{day}$, $t_{50} = 380\text{ days}$ ($1.04\text{ yr}$) and $t_{90} = 1,635\text{ days}$ ($4.48\text{ yr}$).
   - Across the 15 biweekly survey rounds (`12/12/2025` to `06/26/2026`, $196\text{ days}$ elapsed), cumulative settlement has already reached **$-0.61\text{ in}$** at interior point **MP-7** (FTG-C7) and **$-0.58\text{ in}$** at **MP-6** (FTG-C6) vs. **$-0.31\text{ in}$** at corner **MP-12** (FTG-C12), with measured differential settlement already at **$0.23\text{ in}$** between adjacent columns (MP-7 vs. MP-3 and MP-8 vs. MP-12) and **$0.30\text{ in}$** across the footprint.
   - The biweekly settlement rate at MP-7 has monotonically accelerated from $-0.02\text{ to }-0.03\text{ in/round}$ ($-0.0021\text{ in/day}$) in Dec 2025–Jan 2026 to $-0.06\text{ in/round}$ ($-0.0043\text{ in/day}$) in May–Jun 2026 and **$-0.07\text{ in/round}$ ($-0.0050\text{ in/day} = -1.83\text{ in/yr}$)** in Round 15 (`06/12/2026` $\to$ `06/26/2026`), confirming active virgin clay consolidation on a concave-downward trajectory that will breach $1.00\text{ in}$ within $\sim 78\text{ days}$.

---

### Formal Verification Disposition & Required Deliverables Before Closure

- **Disposition as of `07/20/2026`:** **`Item 051: NOT VERIFIED`** (Register Status: **Open**). As of `07/20/2026`, the list of Block C foundation or structural loading operations releasable as conforming is **empty / zero**.
- **Deliverables Required Prior to Closing Item 051 and Responsible Parties:**
  1. **Revised, PE-Sealed Settlement Calculation (`CB-GEO-007 Rev.1`) — Required from Gregory Nash, PE (Structural Engineer of Record, Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC):** Must complete Sheet 4 with full 1-D primary consolidation ($S_c$), immediate ($S_i$), and 3-D Boussinesq differential settlement calculations across all Block C footings, reconcile the $\text{El. } 740.5\text{ ft}$ vs. $\text{El. } 746.0\text{ ft}$ footing elevation discrepancy with `S-201 Rev.4`, and calibrate time-rate predictions against the 15-round field monitoring data.
  2. **PE-Sealed Block C Foundation Remediation / Underpinning Design & Structural Distress Assessment — Required from Gregory Nash, PE (Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC) in coordination with Alden Roscombe, PE / Harlan V. Kelbrook, PE (Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.):** Must provide a sealed underpinning/remediation design transferring Block C column loads through the compressible Stratum 2 clay into the dense Stratum 3 SW-GW stratum below $\text{El. } 720.0\text{ ft}$ to arrest total and differential settlements within the $1.0\text{ in}$ / $0.5\text{ in}$ tolerances, together with a structural assessment of existing Block C framing, masonry partitions, and the shared Grid Line 6 podium interface for the $0.61\text{ in}$ total / $0.23\text{–}0.30\text{ in}$ differential movement already experienced.
  3. **Updated Field Settlement Monitoring Reports (Rounds 16+ Post-`06/26/2026`) and Weekly Survey Cadence — Required from Dennis Halloran, PLS (Survey Party Chief), Marcus Whitfield (Superintendent), and Steven Kendrow (Project Executive), Rowan Bay Constructors, Inc.:** Must submit the July 2026 survey rounds (`07/10/2026` Round 16 and `07/24/2026` Round 17), increase survey frequency from biweekly to weekly on MP-1 through MP-12, and maintain the hold on any additional Block C dead-load application until remedial works are verified.
